summary: The change closes the remaining double-settlement paths: reclaim of a processing webhook event is limited to failed events or expired leases, a failing delivery can only release its own claim, and risk settlement effects are now idempotent per Stripe event through the event-keyed ledger key plus a deterministic identity-risk entry id. Integration and unit tests cover the concurrent claim conflict and the retried settlement.

evidence: src/credits.ts:2780-2790 now reclaims a processing event only when lease_expires_at is expired, or when a null lease has updated_at older than the lease window, so a live claim returns stripe_webhook_claim_conflict instead of running settlement again.
src/credits.ts:2859-2866 releases a failed delivery only while the row is still outcome processing and still carries that delivery owner token, so a processed outcome cannot be overwritten.

src/credits.ts:5524-5536 and 5587-5601 skip the remaining risk effects when the event-keyed account_status ledger row already exists, and src/credits.ts:5636-5654 derives the billing_linkedin_identity_risk_events entry_id from the event id plus identity so replays are dropped.

src/billing_postgres_integration_test.ts:1397-1505 delivers the signed risk webhook twice while the first settlement is blocked on the payment intent advisory lock, asserts a 409 conflict for the second delivery, then forces a retried settlement and asserts the ledger and identity-risk row counts stay at one.
